item.title: China passes revised Water Law to strengthen water conservation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- Chinese lawmakers on Friday voted to pass the revised Water Law, which will take effect on March 22, 2027. The revised law consists of nine chapters covering water resources planning, protection, development and utilization, water conservation, river and lake management, water project construction and operation, and legal liability, among other areas. The law calls for prioritizing water conservation, promoting a balanced spatial distribution of water resources, and adopting a systematic approach to water governance, while harnessing the complementary roles of government and market mechanisms. It also stresses comprehensive planning, coordinated management, integrated utilization and efficiency, alongside efforts to address both immediate problems and their root causes. The law further calls for leveraging the multiple functions of water resources and coordinating the management of water resources, aquatic ecosystems, water environments and water-related disasters. China's Water Law was first enacted in 1988 and underwent a major revision in 2002, followed by amendments in 2009 and 2016. The law provides a legal framework for the development, utilization, conservation and protection of water resources, as well as the prevention and control of water-related disasters. China reported continued improvement in its water use efficiency in 2025, according to data from the Ministry of Water Resources. Last year, China's water consumption per 10,000 yuan (about 1,489 U.S. dollars) of gross domestic product (GDP) declined 4.5 percent year on year, while water consumption per 10,000 yuan of industrial added value dropped 7.2 percent, the ministry data showed. China's total water resources reached 2.72 trillion cubic meters in 2025. ■

item.title: China's digital drive delivers inclusive gains to people
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
HANGZHOU, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- For one minute on the main stage of the 2026 World Internet Conference (WIC) Wuzhen Summit in east China, a young man played a gentle piano piece that few realized was performed via a neurally controlled bionic hand, the fruit of a decade of research and development. The performer, surnamed Shi, lost his right hand in an accident at age 12. This year, he was fitted with the bionic hand developed by brain-computer interface (BCI) company BrainCo. "The hand enables independent finger movement through intuitive, low-latency control for precise two-handed piano play," said Shi, whose robotic hand features a human-like covering, at the summit held Nov. 2-5. BCI TECH RESTORES MOBILITY Over the past decade, BrainCo's team has worked with people with limb disabilities, studying their neural data, and "finally developed the sensors and algorithms that made it work," said Han Bicheng, founder and CEO of BrainCo, at the summit's main forum in Wuzhen, Zhejiang Province. The company's products allow people to write, draw and play the piano, and enable people to walk, run and even go rock climbing and surfing, said Han, noting that the company has helped over 10,000 people with limb disabilities across China regain their daily lives. Traditional BCI gear was "too complex and expensive" for daily use given faint brain signals, prompting Han to explore reimagining the tech -- the idea behind BrainCo. Han's start-up mirrors China's BCI industry, where companies are drawing on the country's robust communications networks, cloud computing and smart manufacturing systems to address challenges. RoboCT, another Zhejiang-based company, offers BCI products such as exoskeletons to people with disabilities. "While other robots handle what people don't want to do, exoskeletons empower us to do what we want to do but can't," said Zhang Jiyu, RoboCT's co-founder and chief operations officer. Compared with traditional passive device-assisted methods, rehabilitation speeds up significantly when the brain actively sends signals to drive muscles and bones via BCI tech, said Hong Xuanyu, the company's head of BCI products. Beyond cutting-edge technologies, the summit, which drew about 1,800 delegates from 138 countries and regions, also showed how digital transformation is reaching ordinary households, turning hopes into everyday realities. WATER TOWN'S WISHES COME TRUE In 2014, when the WIC was launched in Wuzhen, Xinhua reporters there asked locals one question: "What do you hope the Internet will bring you?" Some sought more business, some home convenience, others a more connected world. These scenes and comments are exhibited in a photo exhibition of this year's summit, with many of those wishes coming true. "I hope I can choose, order and have fresh vegetables delivered online," wrote Guo Yueming in 2014, who still runs her homestay in the canal town. Back then, she left before 5 a.m. every day to buy fresh ingredients, spending more than an hour on the road and much of the morning washing and preparing them. Now, she places an order on her phone before 10 p.m., and fresh produce arrives at her door by 10 the next morning. "With Internet platforms, guests feel more at ease, and we have less to worry about," said Guo, who can check room availability at a glance on her phone. Visitors, by scanning QR codes on the linens, can see the full laundry journey, number of wash cycles and even pH levels, an indicator of hygiene. At Wuzhen's Xizha Scenic Zone, visitors take turns snapping photos beneath a five-meter circular bamboo tray bearing the name "Wuzhen," framing themselves and the two Chinese characters in the same shot. Few may realize the piece was created by Qian Xinming, a local bamboo-weaving artisan. More than a decade ago, he sat on a bamboo stool outside his small shop in Xizha, splitting bamboo strips and weaving patterns. Passersby glanced in, snapped a photo and moved on, with few stopping to ask about prices or the craft itself. "I want to connect with bamboo-weaving enthusiasts around the world through the Internet," Qian wrote in 2014. Traditional bamboo-weaving culture needs to be shared with the help of new tools, or the craft "would remain trapped here," Qian recalled. Qian's son now uses AI and digital tools to document, preserve and promote bamboo weaving. Their new works have reached dozens of countries and regions. "Artisans, connected by the Internet, can turn traditional patterns into works that speak to contemporary taste and carry them beyond China," said Qian. AI DEVELOPMENT SHOULD AMPLIFY HUMAN VALUE "Today, we don't just discuss the future. We can see it," said John Hoffman, chairman and director of the Global System for Mobile Communications Association Ltd., who dubbed WIC "a small policy conversation" back in 2014. China is demonstrating "how advanced connectivity can become a universal utility like electricity and water," said Hoffman. "The opportunity is to translate this technology and leadership into inclusive prosperity, ensuring that no one is left behind." "The core of AI development should be to amplify human value and empower people," said Xi Dan, senior vice president of China's tech giant Tencent, noting that the company's inclusive AI initiatives have reached seniors, children in rural areas and women. "We aim to make BCI a daily interface for everyone over the next five to 10 years," said Han, who envisions, for instance, helping children with autism speak again and anyone struggling with insomnia get a good night's sleep. "We believe that the more open the underlying network, the warmer the technology, and the deeper the digital foundation, the more dignity ordinary lives can enjoy," said Han. ■

item.title: Xi replies to young Australian students
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping recently replied to 110 young Australian students who had written to him, encouraging them to remain committed to promoting the China-Australia friendship. In his letter dated Oct. 28, Xi said he was pleased to learn that the students recently visited China to take part in the Sino-Australian Collegiate Rowing and Dragon Boat Friendship Challenge, where they competed alongside Chinese university students, engaged in in-depth exchanges, forged friendships that transcended borders, and created wonderful memories together. China and Australia share a longstanding tradition of friendly exchanges, Xi noted, adding that the future of bilateral relations lies with the younger generation. He voiced hope that the Australian students can continue to actively contribute to the cause of friendship between the two countries, serve as torchbearers of the friendship and cooperation between the two countries, and carry forward this friendship from generation to generation. Recently, 110 young Australian students from the University of Sydney and other universities jointly wrote to Xi and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, sharing their experiences of the China trip. They expressed admiration for China's long-lasting history and rich culture, as well as its scientific and technological innovation capabilities. They also voiced their eagerness to help carry forward the bilateral friendship and foster greater mutual understanding. ■

item.title: Xi says a growing China can be partner to help Europe tackle challenges
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- A growing and developing China is not the source of Europe's problems, but a partner that can help Europe address its challenges, said Chinese President Xi Jinping during his meeting with Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker in Beijing on Friday. Xi stressed that China and Europe should focus on areas of cooperation, resolve economic and trade frictions through dialogue and consultation, and achieve win-win results and common development. ■

item.description:

BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping held talks with Gabonese President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema in Beijing on Friday. The two leaders announced the elevation of bilateral relations to a China-Gabon community with a shared future for the new era. ■

item.title: Xi votes in local legislative election in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping cast his ballot at a polling station in Beijing on Friday to elect deputies to a local people's congress. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, voted at the Huairentang polling station of the Zhongnanhai electoral district in Xicheng District to elect deputies to the Xicheng district people's congress. Xi stressed efforts to practice whole-process people's democracy, uphold Party leadership, and strengthen oversight throughout the election process to ensure that deputies who meet the people's expectations are elected. Around 3:30 p.m. Friday, Xi arrived at the polling station, gave his voter registration card to staff for verification, and got a ballot. He cast his ballot after filling it. Noting that the election of deputies to people's congresses is an important foundation for upholding, improving and practicing the people's congress system, Xi underlined the need to give full play to democracy, strictly act in accordance with the law, and ensure that the election is carried out fairly and cleanly. On Friday afternoon, other senior Chinese leaders Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi cast their ballots in person, while Han Zheng entrusted a staff member to vote on his behalf. Former Chinese leader Hu Jintao also entrusted a staff member to vote on his behalf. Friday saw people vote at 13,054 polling stations across Beijing to elect 4,898 new deputies to the people's congresses at the district level and 11,137 deputies to the township-level people's congresses. ■

item.title: Xi holds talks with Sultan of Oman, stressing bilateral cooperation, peace efforts in Middle East
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
Chinese President Xi Jinping holds talks with Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik Al Said of Oman, who is on a state visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 2, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) BEIJING, Nov. 2 (Xinhua) -- President Xi Jinping said on Monday that China stands ready to work with Oman to steer their strategic partnership to a higher level, and to help restore peace and realize lasting stability in the Middle East at an early date. Xi made the remarks during talks with Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik Al Said of Oman, who is on a state visit to China -- the first by Oman's head of state since the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries 48 years ago. The talks constituted an important chapter in the history of China-Oman relations and will inject strong impetus into the development of bilateral ties, Xi said. He said China and Oman should enhance political mutual trust and strengthen exchanges of experience in national governance, while expressing China's support for Oman in safeguarding national independence, sovereignty, security and stability, and in independently exploring a development path suited to its national conditions. The two sides should expand practical cooperation and continuously cement the foundation of mutually beneficial and win-win cooperation, he said, adding that China is committed to promoting high-quality development and expanding high-standard opening up, which will bring greater opportunities to Oman and other countries. China is ready to deepen the synergy of development strategies with Oman and be a stable and reliable partner in the energy sector, a partner with promising potential in investment, and a partner in fostering innovation within advanced technologies, he said. China aims to make bilateral energy cooperation more multi-dimensional and comprehensive, strengthen exchanges in industry, investment, artificial intelligence (AI), science and technology, and people-to-people ties, and join hands on the paths toward development, revitalization, and modernization, Xi said. He also called for efforts to intensify cooperation in such fields as education, tourism, health, media and sports, to continuously substantiate the China-Oman strategic partnership. Xi noted that the Middle East and the Gulf region should not become an arena for major power rivalry or geopolitical conflicts, and that concerted efforts are needed to foster and maintain peace and stability in the region. "China has been actively committed to ending hostilities and promoting peace, aiming to contribute its wisdom and solutions to resolving the regional security predicament," Xi said. China will continue to advocate resolving disputes through political and diplomatic means, and support regional countries in building a common home of good-neighborliness, development, security and cooperation, he added. China is ready to strengthen communication and coordination with Oman and other Arab states and Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries to jointly work for the early restoration of peace and tranquility in the region and the realization of lasting stability, Xi said. Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik said that Oman firmly adheres to the one-China principle and supports China in safeguarding its national sovereignty and territorial integrity. He expressed hope that this visit will serve as a new starting point to explore more cooperation opportunities with China, and build a future-oriented partnership and promote greater development of bilateral relations. Stressing that China has been Oman's largest trading partner for many years and Chinese enterprises' investment in Oman has kept growing, Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik said Oman is ready to synergize development strategies with China and strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, industry, infrastructure, AI, science and technology, and other fields. He said Oman highly appreciates China's just position on the Middle East issue and stands ready to maintain close coordination with China to uphold international law, advocate for the peaceful resolution of disputes, and jointly promote security and stability in the region and beyond. After their talks, the two leaders jointly witnessed the signing of cooperation documents covering areas including industrial and supply chains, green development and digital finance. During the visit, the two sides issued a joint statement on deepening the China-Oman strategic partnership. Prior to the talks, Xi held a welcome ceremony for Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik in the Great Hall of the People.
